note: The Robot Transformation Benchmark: a FIXED instrument for the amend/generate loop, held separate from Design-Bench. Design-Bench measures prompt -> composed body (a regression gate that must stay green). This measures transformation of an EXISTING robot plus expressivity on machine classes we cannot yet express, so several cases are expected-red by construction and are marked `expect: fail` with the reason. Grade every case on its own acceptance criteria; never average across sections. Baselines are MuJoCo Menagerie models, referenced by their cached relative path; all 55 referenced models were confirmed importable by scratchpad/import_sweep.py (62/63 imported, see build/import_sweep.json).

sections.A_local_edit: One named part changes; every other part must stay byte-identical and both joint interfaces must survive.
sections.B_structural: Topology or multi-part change; out-of-scope parts still must not drift.
sections.C_expressivity: Non-animal machine classes. Probes the closed 23-role vocabulary; expected-red until the part language is opened.
sections.D_intake: Malformed, ambiguous or keyframe-less input. Correct behaviour is a TYPED actionable failure or an honest partial, never a silent guess.

grading.preserved_regions_exact: Named parts must be byte-identical in the re-exported gene/MJCF.
grading.interfaces_survive: Each listed interface keeps its parent/child attachment and its transform within 1e-6 m.
grading.verdict_not_worse: gait_quality.classify verdict on the revision is no worse than on the baseline, using the revision's OWN tuned/learned controller.
grading.invalidations_reported: The change-impact report must name at least the listed rechecks; missing a safety-critical one is a hard fail.
grading.typed_failure: Failure must be a structured report naming the cause and a next action, not a raw exception.

cases.request: make the lower leg segments 30% longer, from 0.213 m to 0.277 m
cases.acceptance: all four calves measure 0.277 +/- 0.002 m; feet still attached at the calf tip; hips unchanged; verdict not worse

cases.request: lengthen only the FRONT thighs by 20%, leave the rear thighs alone
cases.acceptance: front thighs 0.256 m, rear 0.213 m; asymmetry is deliberate and must survive re-grounding
cases.why: the asymmetric fore/hind leg axis the co-design literature randomises; also the axis whose change broke 12 tests

cases.request: make the calves 40% thicker without changing their length
cases.acceptance: radius x1.4, length unchanged; mass and inertia re-derived, not copied

cases.request: raise the standing height 15% by lengthening the legs
cases.acceptance: standing height +15% via LINK LENGTH; no spacer/filler part introduced; body untouched
cases.why: the user's explicit requirement: taller must not mean a block inserted into the legs

cases.request: extend the forearm by 100 mm to reach further across the bench
cases.acceptance: reach envelope grows; wrist stack still attached at the forearm tip; joint-2 torque demand recomputed

cases.request: the elbow joint stalls under load — fit a higher-torque actuator
cases.acceptance: a real catalog part is selected whose envelope fits the housing; mass/BOM delta reported; NO invented catalog row

cases.request: add a wrist camera mount without losing the gripper
cases.acceptance: sensor mount present at the wrist; gripper still attached with its transform unchanged

cases.request: make link 3 lighter without losing stiffness
cases.acceptance: link-3 mass drops with the interfaces preserved; the claim is derived from the revised solid, not asserted

cases.request: increase reach 15% while staying inside the existing actuators' torque
cases.acceptance: either a revision that meets both, or an honest report that torque is the binding constraint
cases.why: a case where the correct answer may be 'no' — an honest infeasibility report scores as a pass

cases.request: lengthen the fingers to grip a 90 mm tall bottle
cases.acceptance: stroke still closes fully; fingers do not self-intersect through their range

cases.request: widen the stance for better roll stability
cases.acceptance: hip mount offsets widen; leg geometry itself unchanged; stance_aspect_w_h improves

cases.request: fit larger foot pads for soft ground
cases.acceptance: contact pad grows in the ground plane only; standing height re-derived so the pad rests ON the floor
cases.why: guards the recorded 'boot 38 mm below the contact surface' defect

cases.request: mount a 6-DOF arm on its back
cases.acceptance: 12 -> 18 actuated DOF; legs byte-identical; carried arm mass excluded from the stance ratio; still walks

cases.request: give it a third arm
cases.acceptance: three distinct arms present and non-intersecting; balance re-checked; the answer may legitimately be a warning that payload is exceeded
cases.why: the user asked for exactly this as the bar for amend capability

cases.request: make it taller
cases.acceptance: height increases through LINK LENGTH and a re-derived stance; a spacer/filler segment is a HARD FAIL

cases.request: remove the left arm and rebalance
cases.acceptance: left-arm chain gone; COM shift reported; right arm untouched

cases.request: add a tall sensor mast on top
cases.acceptance: mast present; the legged stance rule must NOT reject it as too-tall (carried mass is not stance)
cases.why: regression guard for the carried-geoms fix

cases.request: add a second gripper on a Y-splitter at the wrist
cases.acceptance: two end-effectors, both reachable, not intersecting through the wrist range

cases.request: add a middle pair of legs to make it a hexapod
cases.acceptance: 6 ground-reaching chains; the gait engine handles the new leg count without a per-count special case

cases.request: put this arm on a mobile base so it can drive
cases.acceptance: base_mount changes from table to free with a driving base; the arm chain is unchanged; verdict rubric switches to the DRIVING one honestly

cases.request: a 3-axis cartesian gantry: two vertical columns carrying a horizontal beam, a carriage on the beam, and a vertical Z ram on the carriage
cases.acceptance: 3 prismatic DOF along X, Y and Z with real travel limits; a rectangular work envelope
cases.why: no gantry/column/beam/rail/carriage role in _ROLES; joints carry no axis or limits through submit_design

cases.request: a SCARA arm: two revolute links in a horizontal plane plus a vertical prismatic Z at the wrist
cases.acceptance: 2R + 1P with both revolutes about Z and a limited prismatic stroke
cases.why: mixed revolute/prismatic chain with per-joint axes is not expressible

cases.request: a delta robot: a fixed top plate with three arms driving a shared moving platform
cases.acceptance: three arms converging on ONE shared platform
cases.why: STRUCTURAL LIMIT, not vocabulary: RobotGene is a tree, and a delta is a closed kinematic chain. Needs MuJoCo equality constraints, so this case stays red until parallel mechanisms are modelled at all

cases.request: a tracked loader: two continuous tracks and a front loader boom with a bucket
cases.acceptance: track-driven locomotion (not discrete wheels) plus a 2-link boom and a bucket
cases.why: no track role; tracks are also a contact model we do not have

cases.request: a rotating turret on a fixed pedestal, with a pitching barrel
cases.acceptance: yaw about Z at the pedestal, pitch about Y at the turret, both with limits
cases.why: no turret/pedestal role; nothing may mount at an arbitrary point on a parent

cases.request: an excavator arm: boom, stick and bucket on a slewing house
cases.acceptance: slew + 3 pitching joints with real limits and a bucket end-effector
cases.why: no boom/stick/bucket/house role, and the chain needs per-joint axes and asymmetric limits that submit_design cannot carry

cases.request: a linear rail with a carriage that travels along it
cases.acceptance: one prismatic DOF with a stroke that matches the rail's length
cases.why: smallest possible expressivity probe: one prismatic joint with a limit

cases.request: a quadrotor: four rotors on arms around a central body
cases.acceptance: four rotor mounts in a symmetric cross; honest statement that thrust is not simulated
cases.why: no rotor role, and flight is out of tier — the honest out-of-tier answer is the pass condition, not a fake hover

cases.acceptance: a typed report saying this is an include-fragment, not a standalone model, naming the real model file to use
cases.why: measured: raises ValueError('keyframe scissors: invalid qpos size, expected 0, got 24')

cases.acceptance: detect that the file holds SEVERAL robots and ask which one, or return a typed multi-robot report
cases.why: measured: flattens into one 65-segment 64-actuator 0.67 kg 'robot'

cases.acceptance: robot_class == humanoid, and NO invented rest pose (h1.xml ships no keyframe)
cases.why: measured: classifies as mobile_base — 12 of 12 bipeds in the corpus are misclassified

cases.request: import this hand
cases.acceptance: robot_class == manipulator
cases.why: measured: four fingers count as four limbs, so it classifies as a quadruped

cases.request: import this quadruped
cases.acceptance: imports as a quadruped with no rest_pose (this model ships no keyframe) and is NOT posed with straight legs by default

cases.request: import it and confirm the geometry is mine, not a lookalike
cases.acceptance: 13 segments, 12 actuated, mass within 25% of 15.2 kg, every segment carrying source_mesh geometry, and the source 'home' stance
cases.why: the intake fidelity floor; currently measured 13/12/15.21 kg/13 meshed/8 posed

cases.acceptance: either flag that this is a sub-assembly of a larger robot, or report the 2-segment 120 kg result with that mass called out as implausible for its size
cases.why: measured: 2 segments, 120 kg, accepted silently
